You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object. KNOWN BUG: When a child of the dialog uses autoFocus, focus does not return to the element that opened the dialog after it closes. Rules: - Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no". - A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no". - Wording does not matter; the behaviour does. - For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure. === REVIEW 1 FINDINGS === - [blocking] Tabs: when a stateful child inside TabList removes the selected Tab, no tab keeps tabIndex 0 and the list cannot be reached by Tab. `TabList` only recomputes `stop` in its own layout effect, which does not run when the child re-renders alone. Repro (`P5`): `A…` where `Dyn` hides `` on click. After hiding, `A` has `tabindex="-1"`. Violates T2, T4 and the README line "Only the selected tab is in the tab order." A parent-driven removal (rerender) works, which is why the basic tests miss it. - [blocking] Dialog: `FOCUSABLE` matches `input:not([disabled])`, which includes ``. Repro (`D3hidden`, `dialog2`): ``. Initial focus lands on the dialog, not b1 (D2). Tab sequence was `b1, b2, b2, b2`: Tab from the last button stays on b2 because the wrap target is the hidden input, which cannot take focus. That is a keyboard trap for forward Tab (D3). - [blocking] Combobox: removing the active option from `options` while open leaves `aria-activedescendant` pointing at a missing id. Repro (`C3 dangling`): ArrowDown twice to Cherry, then rerender with Cherry removed. `aria-activedescendant` = `«r9»-option-cherry`, and `getElementById` returns null. Violates C3 ("never points at a hidden option" and "equals the active option's id"). Fix would be to clear or re-derive activeValue against the current `enabled` list. - [minor] Combobox: with the listbox open and no active option, Enter calls `preventDefault` and blocks form submission. A press that starts on the backdrop and ends inside the dialog still closes it. Not in the spec. Click-start-inside and drag-out-of-dialog cases were reproduced as not closing. === REVIEW 2 FINDINGS === - [blocking] Dialog backdrop flags are never reset after a close the parent ignores. `pressStartedOnBackdrop` and `pressEndedOnBackdrop` stay true from a completed backdrop press, so a later click with no mousedown still calls onOpenChange(false). Repro: `await user.click(backdrop)` with a no-op onOpenChange, then `fireEvent.click(backdrop)`. Result: `expected "spy" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`. Real browsers always send mousedown first, so the practical impact is small. Fix: reset both refs in handleBackdropClick or on the next close. - [blocking] Tabs under StrictMode: `onValueChange` fires twice on mount for an uncontrolled Tabs with no defaultValue. The TabList layout effect's `select(first)` runs again on the double-invoked effect. Repro: `render(…two tabs…)` gives `[['a'],['a']]`. Without StrictMode it is `[['a']]`. This breaks T1 "called only when it differs". Dev-only, but the criterion is explicit. - [minor] Combobox: a click on the input does not open the listbox, so options=[] shows "No results" only after ArrowDown or typing. The criteria do not name a click-to-open mechanism. Not a failure of the stated criteria. - [minor] Combobox: Enter with no active option and nothing selected lets the enclosing form submit (native default is not prevented). Enter with an active option does not submit. See OPEN QUESTIONS. - [minor] Dialog: `description=""` renders an empty div and points aria-describedby at it. Not reproduced against D1, which says "when given". - [minor] Tabs: when controlled and the parent ignores onValueChange, arrow keys move DOM focus to another tab while the tab stop stays on the selected tab. Not in the criteria; not checked against the WAI pattern. - [minor] Dialog nesting: two dialogs mounted in the same render leave focus on the outer dialog, so Escape goes to the outer one. This is documented in the README, so it is not a finding. === IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) === GOAL: Fix six reproduced defects in the existing Tabs/Dialog/Combobox implementation and add a regression test for each.
